title: Kafka Rebalancing: Deep Dive Notes
summary: A dense study-notes handbook on Kafka consumer group rebalancing: triggers, assignment strategies, eager vs cooperative protocols, static membership, zombie fencing, and practical tuning.

chapters.title: Consumer Groups & Why Rebalancing Exists
points: Consumer group = set of consumers sharing a group.id; partitions of a topic are divided among members (not replicated)
Group Coordinator: a broker (leader of __consumer_offsets partition for the group) that manages membership via heartbeat requests
Group Leader: one consumer member computes the assignment plan; coordinator just distributes it — assignment logic lives client-side
Max of one consumer owns a partition per group; ownership is the invariant rebalancing preserves
Consumer sends JoinGroup → coordinator picks leader → leader sends SyncGroup with plan → members get their assignment
Offsets are committed per (group, topic, partition); rebalancing without committing causes duplicates or losses
Generation number: incremented every rebalance; every member's requests carry it so stale members are rejected
Rebalancing = stopping-the-world by default: all members drop partitions, halt processing, then rejoin
Livelock risk: if one consumer hangs but keeps heartbeats, group can't proceed — max.poll.interval.ms guards this
Rebalancing is triggered client-side via membership changes, not broker pushes — coordinator learns via session timeouts
Key mental model: rebalancing trades availability of the whole group to fix membership of one member

chapters.title: What Triggers a Rebalance
points: Member leaves: consumer.close() or LeaveGroupRequest (e.g., clean shutdown, SIGTERM handled by the client)
Session timeout: no heartbeat within session.timeout.ms (broker-side config) → member evicted, rebalance starts
Poll timeout: no poll() within max.poll.interval.ms (client config) → consumer proactively leaves the group
Heartbeat interval: heartbeats sent by background thread at heartbeat.interval.ms (must be < 1/3 session timeout)
New member joins: scale-out, app deploy, or consumer started with same group.id
Subscription change: any member changes its subscribed topics/pattern — group-wide rebalance
Topic/partition changes: partitions added to a subscribed topic or topic deleted
Coordinator change: broker holding the group dies → new coordinator may need to reform the group
Config confusion: session.timeout.ms is broker-side (group.max.session.timeout.ms ceiling); max.poll.interval.ms is client-side — tune both, they fail differently
Docker/K8s gotcha: rolling deploys without graceful close trigger LeaveGroup; SIGKILL instead triggers the full session timeout wait
Diagnosis: watch log for 'Preparing to rebalance group ... with old member id' and generation bumps in JMX (kafka.consumer:type=consumer-coordinator-metrics)
Every rebalance pauses ALL consumption — so a flaky member is a tax on the whole group

chapters.title: The Eager Rebalance Protocol (Classic)
points: Eager = 'give up everything first': all members revoke ALL partitions before requesting new ones
Flow: everyone rejoins (JoinGroup) → leader computes plan → SyncGroup → members fetch their (possibly same) partitions
Whole group's consumption stops for the duration — duration includes the slowest member's poll/commit cleanup
OnPartitionRevoked fires for every partition, even ones the consumer will get right back
Commit-on-revoke pattern: commit offsets for revoked partitions inside the revoke callback to avoid reprocessing
Straggler problem: one slow or GC-paused consumer delays every member's rejoin (JoinGroup waits for all)
Request timeout during rebalance: if the group takes too long, members get RebalanceInProgress or commit failures
Shuffle cost: Range and RoundRobin assignors often move partitions between members even when membership barely changed — churn kills cache/page warmth
Message loss/dup window: processing in-flight when partitions are revoked must be fenced by generation checks on commit
Kafka 2.4+ still defaults the protocol to EAGER for Range/RoundRobin — cooperative requires opt-in
Rule of thumb: eager rebalance cost grows with group size × partition count, not just with the change size

chapters.title: Range & RoundRobin Assignors
points: RangeAssignor (default): per-topic, partitions sorted, consumers sorted lexicographically; first C consumers get the remainder
Range flaw: with many topics, the lexicographically-first consumers always get the extra partition — skew accumulates per topic
Example: 5 partitions, 2 consumers, Range → A gets 3, B gets 2; with 10 topics A gets +10 partitions total
CooperativeAssignableStickyRangeAssignor: range's logic made cooperative-compatible (3.0+ renamed to RangeAssignor handling COOPERATIVE)
RoundRobinAssignor: all partitions pooled across topics, dealt out cyclically to members — even spread
RoundRobin requires all group members to subscribe to the same topics, else it degenerates
Both Range and RoundRobin are EAGER: full revoke on every rebalance
StickyAssignor: minimizes partition movement between rebalances while staying balanced — but still eager protocol
Comparison lens: balance (RR best) vs fairness per topic (Range) vs movement minimization (Sticky)
Sticky is only as good as its inputs — unequal subscriptions force it to break stickiness
Tie-breakers are member-id-based: changing member IDs (e.g., on restart) can reshuffle a 'sticky' plan
Real-world note: default Range + eager is why legacy groups see heavy churn on every deploy

chapters.title: Cooperative-Sticky: The Incremental Protocol
points: Cooperative rebalancing (KIP-429, Kafka 2.4): members revoke only the partitions actually being reassigned; rest keep processing
Two round trip: first SyncGroup tells members what to revoke, revocations happen, second round finalizes new assignments
No global stop-the-world: unaffected members never pause; group throughput mostly preserved
CooperativeStickyAssignor: enabled via partition.assignment.strategy=org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.CooperativeStickyAssignor
Sticky inherited: assignment minimizes movement between rebalances AND uses the incremental protocol
OnPartitionsRevoked now fires only for partitions truly lost; use onPartitionsLost for partitions owned by someone else (crash case)
Consumer code gotcha: must not call poll() with partitions you haven't been assigned; callbacks must be cooperative-safe

Rolling upgrade path: consumers must switch protocols in a specific order — set strategy on all members across two restarts (all → EAGER then all → COOPERATIVE) or you hit inconsistent protocol errors
Both old and new members present = INCONSISTENT_GROUP_PROTOCOL; plan the migration, don't mix protocols
Big win: rolling restarts and scale-ups cause only incremental movement, preserving local caches and fetch buffers
Incremental cooperative also reduces 'rebalance storms' since partial failures don't wipe all state
Trade-off: plan computation is more complex and stickiness heuristics can occasionally yield slightly imbalanced assignments

chapters.title: Static Membership (KIP-345)
points: Problem: consumer restart gets a NEW member.id → coordinator sees leave/join → full rebalance on every restart, even with same identity
Fix: group.instance.id (e.g., pod-0, host-a) gives a stable identity; server-side member.id tracked against it
Behavior: consumer with same group.instance.id rejoins without triggering a rebalance — it just reclaims its partitions
Config: group.instance.id (client) + session.timeout.ms raised (e.g., 45s–5min) so restarts fit inside the window
LeaveGroup from a static member is IGNORED by the coordinator by default — deliberate stop won't rebalance until session timeout
Consequence: you must shut down gracefully and wait, or accept the session-timeout delay for partition reassignment
Best fit: stateful apps (Kafka Streams, k8s StatefulSets) with stable pod names/identities
Anti-pattern: autoscaling or dynamic pools reusing instance ids → zombies or overlap errors: 'member id X fenced by instance id Y' (FENCED_INSTANCE_ID)
Static membership + sticky/cooperative-sticky = near-zero partition movement on restarts: same instance gets same partitions
Bonus: offsets and internal state (e.g., Streams standbys) stay warm — big tail-latency win
Monitor: fenced instance id errors indicate duplicate identity assignment, not normal rebalancing

chapters.title: Zombies, Fencing & Generation/Epoch Guardrails
points: Zombie = a consumer believed dead by the group (timed out or left) that keeps processing and committing offsets
Classic hazard: zombie commits stale offsets after another member already reprocessed the partition → duplicates or lost writes
Generation number fencing: commits carry (group, generation, member.id); coordinator rejects commits with a stale generation via ILLEGAL_GENERATION
Zombie fencing only works at commit time — in-flight side effects (DB writes, API calls) are NOT fenced by Kafka
Real fencing needs downstream: transactional id + producer epoch for exactly-once (KIP-98), or external idempotency/version checks
FencedInstanceException (KIP-345): static member rejoining with a new runtime member.id fences the old one instantly
Consumer heartbeat thread detects ILLEGAL_GENERATION / UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID → commits fail → consumer must drop work and rejoin
Pattern: pause processing on revoke callback until onPartitionsAssigned re-grants — avoids processing unowned partitions
Transactional consumers: read_committed + transactional producers make the zombie's writes invisible via LSO/abort markers
Streams analogue: task-level fencing via transactional producer epoch; old thread crashes with ProducerFencedException
Timeout tuning vs zombies: shorter session.timeout fences faster but risks spurious rebalances under GC pauses
Key insight: Kafka fences OFFSET COMMITS reliably; everything else (external effects) needs your own idempotency design

chapters.title: Tuning & Common Mistakes
points: Mistake: processing > max.poll.interval.ms → consumer leaves group → rebalance loop; fix by lowering max.poll.records or raising interval
Mistake: session.timeout.ms set below group.min.session.timeout.ms or above max on broker → client defaults silently applied
Mistake: long GC pauses misread as dead members; use cooperative + moderate session timeout instead of ultra-short timeouts
Mistake: committing inside onPartitionsRevoked with an old generation → commit fails; handle CommitFailedException gracefully
Mistake: heavy onClose work in callbacks — revoke/assign callbacks run on the poll thread and block the rebalance for everyone
Mistake: mixing protocols (one member on cooperative-sticky, others eager) → INCONSISTENT_GROUP_PROTOCOL, group won't form
Mistake: Kafka Streams custom assignment: enable cooperative via protocol field on StreamsConfig ( Streams 2.6+ supports COOPERATIVE) — must not mix with EAGER deployments
Tuning: max.poll.records down + longer max.poll.interval up for slow processing; heartbeat.interval.ms = session.timeout/3
Tuning: raise session.timeout.ms + static membership for K8s rolling deploys; use terminationGracePeriod > session timeout
Monitoring: rebalance rate, rebalance latency (time in PreparingRebalance/CompletingRebalance), commit failure count, generation number churn
Idempotency: design consumers so a reprocessed record is safe — dedup keys, upserts, or transactions; rebalances guarantee at-least-once
Checklist: cooperative-sticky assignor + static ids + sane timeouts + idempotent effects + graceful shutdown = resilient group

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet & Decision Summary
points: Pick assignor: CooperativeStickyAssignor for almost everything; Sticky if stuck on eager; Range only for legacy compatibility
Pick membership: static group.instance.id for stable/stateful deployments; dynamic for true autoscaling pools
Rebalance triggers recap: join, leave, session timeout, poll timeout, subscription change, partition/topic change, coordinator failover
Protocol recap: eager = revoke-all stop-the-world; cooperative = incremental revoke via two SyncGroup rounds
Fencing recap: generation/member.id guard commits; producer epoch guards transactions; FENCED_INSTANCE_ID guards static identities
Golden configs: heartbeat.interval.ms ≈ session.timeout/3; max.poll.interval > worst-case poll cycle; session.timeout generous with static membership
Migration recipe: step 1 roll out with protocol=EAGER (or none), step 2 roll all members to COOPERATIVE — never mixed
Deploy recipe: static ids + cooperative-sticky + graceful close (leave via API when intentional) + wait or accept timeout
Symptom map: rebalance loop → poll interval; commit failures → generation changes; duplicates → zombie or missing commit-on-revoke
Trade-off table: eager (simple, disruptive) vs cooperative (complex plan, minimal disruption); dynamic (elastic, rebalances on restart) vs static (stable, sticky, needs careful shutdown)
Cost model: rebalance pain ∝ members × partitions × (revoke + rejoin + re-fetch warmup) — cooperative and sticky shrink every term
Final rule: design for rebalances as routine events — they WILL happen; make consumers idempotent, callbacks fast, and identities stable
